fullPassage: If you had a ten-year-old listen to some bandstand from the fifties, or even a mainstream rap video from the eighties or nineties, then showed them the best of what was being offered today, they'd never listen to that old thing again. And yet, when they grew up, they might still listen to that music and play old games, and might even prefer them to whatever newer and greater thing came out in their twenties and thirties. Why? I hypothesize that our tastes and values, especially when it pertains to entertainment, have to do with the core memories we form as children, the stuff that wows us, that we've never seen before, that takes our breath away. These memories serve as the foundational bedrock for our understanding of the world and our nostalgia for the 'old days'. This is nothing groundbreaking. There's plenty of others who have said this first and backed it up. It only makes sense that the people we idolize - athletes, musicians, movie stars - still hold our attention and appreciation as we grow old, and that the next wave can't hold up through our more experienced, more cynical, and less forgiving eyes. The same sense of wonder that inspires us as children, when we are so full of hope and possibility, is the one we ignore and put down as we grow older and become more focused on routine and responsibilities. The only difference is timing.

I hypothesize that our tastes and values, especially when it pertains to entertainment, have to do with __________, the stuff that wows us, that we've never seen before, that takes our breath away. These memories serve as the foundational bedrock for our understanding of the world and our nostalgia for the 'old days'. This is nothing groundbreaking. There's plenty of others who have said this first and backed it up. It only makes sense that the people we idolize - athletes, musicians, movie stars - still hold our attention and appreciation as we grow old, and that the next wave can't hold up through our more experienced, more cynical, and less forgiving eyes. The same sense of wonder that inspires us as children, when we are so full of hope and possibility, is the one we ignore and put down as we grow older and become more focused on routine and responsibilities. The only difference is timing.

❌ ② the amount of money we spend on entertainment — 본문에 언급 없음

questions.stem:
다음 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

If you had a ten-year-old listen to some bandstand from the fifties, or even a mainstream rap video from the eighties or nineties, then showed them the best of what was being offered today, they'd never listen to that old thing again.

(B) These memories serve as the foundational bedrock for our understanding of the world and our nostalgia for the 'old days'.

(C) There's plenty of others who have said this first and backed it up.

(A) Why? I hypothesize that our tastes and values, especially when it pertains to entertainment, have to do with the core memories we form as children, the stuff that wows us, that we've never seen before, that takes our breath away.

det.korean: Why?라는 물음 뒤에 (A)에서 바로 가설(I hypothesize...)을 제시하고, (B)에서 그 핵심기억(memories)을 'These memories'로 받아 '토대(bedrock)'가 된다고 설명하며, (C)에서 '다른 사람들도 이미 이 주장을 먼저 말하고 뒷받침했다(backed it up)'고 이어지므로 (A)-(B)-(C) 순서가 가장 자연스럽다.
det.analysis:
(A) — Why?에 대한 답으로 가설(I hypothesize)과 core memories 개념 제시, 도입부 바로 뒤에 와야 함
(B) — (A)의 memories를 that이 아닌 'These memories'로 받아 이어 설명, (A) 다음에 와야 함
(C) — (A)·(B)에서 제시한 주장을 'this'로 받아 다른 사람들도 뒷받침(backed it up)했다고 마무리, (B) 다음에 와야 함
←정답: (A)-(B)-(C)
det.tip: Why? → I hypothesize, core memories(A) → These memories(B) → have said this first, backed it up(C)
